corlea-trackway: A centre protecting a 2,000-year-old oak road built across the bog, the only one of its kind in Europe.
glendeer-pet-farm: An animal farm open to visitors, with goats, lambs, birds and an indoor playground.
mullaghmeen-forest: A large planted broadleaf forest, with trails and views over Lough Derravaragh.
kilbeggan-distillery: The world's oldest licensed distillery (1757), with a working steam mill and tastings.
athlone-castle: A 12th-century Norman castle on the River Shannon, with an interactive museum about the Siege of Athlone.
belvedere-house-gardens: An 18th-century country house with gardens, the "Jealous Wall" folly and family events all year round.
tullamore-dew-experience: The Tullamore D.E.W. whiskey visitor centre in a 19th-century warehouse, with guided tastings.
charleville-forest-castle: A 19th-century neo-Gothic castle surrounded by ancient oak woodland, with tours and events.
lough-boora-discovery-park: A park of regenerated boglands with outdoor sculptures, walking and cycling trails and rare birds.
birr-castle-demesne: The Parsons' scientific estate with award-winning gardens, the giant 19th-century telescope and a science centre.
clonmacnoise: One of medieval Europe's most important monasteries, on the banks of the River Shannon, with round towers and high crosses.
slieve-bloom-mountains: Mountains of bogland and forest between Laois and Offaly, with trails, waterfalls and panoramic viewpoints.
abbeyleix-heritage-house: A heritage centre telling the story of planned Georgian Abbeyleix and of the local carpet industry.
timahoe-round-tower: A 12th-century round tower considered one of Ireland's most beautiful, with a richly decorated doorway.
heywood-gardens: Formal 18th/19th-century gardens with terraces, a lake and the famous circular "secret garden".
emo-court: An 18th-century neoclassical mansion with gardens and a lake designed by Capability Brown; free entry.
rock-of-dunamase: A ruined Norman fortress on a rocky outcrop, with 360° views across the Laois countryside.
banna-strand: A long beach of golden sand north of Tralee, with dunes and waters ideal for surfing and swimming.
muckross-abbey: A 15th-century Franciscan abbey with a cloister and a huge central yew tree, in the heart of the national park.
gallarus-oratory: An early Christian dry-stone oratory, over 1,200 years old, shaped like an upturned boat.
derrynane-house: The house of Daniel O'Connell, the Liberator, within a coastal park with a beach and subtropical gardens.
kerry-cliffs: Cliffs over 300 metres high with views of Skellig Michael, on the Skellig Ring.
valentia-island: An island linked by bridge and ferry, with dinosaur footprints, subtropical gardens and the Cromwell Point lighthouse.
skellig-michael: A UNESCO World Heritage Site: a 6th-century monastery atop a rocky island in the Atlantic, a Star Wars filming location.
doneraile-park: An 18th-century landscaped park with deer, trails and a playground — free entry.
